days.title: The Sanctity of a Muslim
days.question: What are the limits of a Muslim's sanctity, and what are his rights over me?
days.principle: All of a Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his blood, his wealth and his honour. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him, forsake him, hand him over, belittle him or expose his faults.

misconception.peopleSay: Covering a Muslim's faults means I never object to him, even while he is still committing the sin.
misconception.correct: Covering applies to a sin that has ended, and objecting applies to a sin that is being committed; covering does not contradict objecting to him privately.

days.action: Choose one of a Muslim's rights mentioned in the hadith (such as visiting the sick, returning a greeting or accepting an invitation) and do it today.
lesson: Islam was very strict about the sanctity of a Muslim's blood, wealth and honour; the Prophet ﷺ said they are as sacred as the day of 'Arafah in the sacred land in the sacred month. Allah legislated retribution (qisas) for deliberate killing to deter anyone thinking of killing, and said there is life in retribution. The Prophet ﷺ said the first thing to be judged between people on the Day of Resurrection is bloodshed, and even merely pointing a weapon at your brother brings the curse of the angels. In Surat al-Hujurat, Allah forbade mockery, defamation, insulting nicknames, suspicion, spying and backbiting. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him or leave him to someone who harms him, and whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection. A Muslim has rights over his brother, such as returning the greeting, visiting the sick, following the funeral and accepting the invitation.

quiz.question: Someone saw his Muslim brother being harmed and was able to defend him, but left him. What did he violate?
options: He violated the right of brotherhood that a Muslim does not forsake his brother or hand him over
It's only recommended, not obligatory at all
quiz.explanation: Meaning: he does not leave him with someone who harms him or in what harms him; rather he supports him and defends him.

quiz.question: You saw one person who committed a sin in the past and it is over, and another committing a sin in front of you now. What do you do?
options: Cover the first, and object to the second
Object to the first and cover the second
quiz.explanation: Covering applies to a sin that has ended, and objecting applies to a sin that is being committed.

quiz.question: What is the first thing to be judged between people on the Day of Resurrection?
options: Bloodshed, which shows how great the sanctity of a Muslim's blood is

askTheBook: What are the rights of a Muslim over a Muslim?
Why was Islam so strict about the sanctity of blood?
When do I cover a Muslim's fault and when do I object?

days.title: Support Your Brother, and Beware of Backbiting
days.question: What does it mean to support my brother when he is the wrongdoer? And what exactly is backbiting?
days.principle: Backbiting (ghibah) is a major sin: mentioning a person in his absence with what he dislikes, even if it is true of him, whether by speech, writing, gesture or hint.

misconception.peopleSay: As long as what I say about the person is true, it isn't backbiting.
misconception.correct: Backbiting is mentioning your brother with what he dislikes: if what you say is true of him, you have backbitten him, and if it is not true of him, you have slandered him.

days.action: If you have reconciled with someone you had fallen out with, be the first to greet them today; the Prophet ﷺ said: «وخيرهما الذي يبدأ بالسلام».
lesson: The Prophet ﷺ said: support your brother whether he is the wrongdoer or the wronged. When the Companions were surprised, he told them that supporting the wrongdoer means stopping him from wrongdoing. The believers are like a building whose parts support one another, and like one body: if one limb complains, the whole body suffers. That is why the Prophet ﷺ forbade envying, hating and turning away from one another, forbade cutting off relations for more than three nights, and said the better of the two is the one who greets first. Then the book says backbiting is a major sin: mentioning your brother in his absence with something he dislikes, even if it is true of him. The Quran depicted it in the ugliest image: eating your brother's flesh when he is dead. Even so, there are specific cases in which backbiting is permissible for a valid purpose, such as seeking redress, asking for a fatwa and warning against harm.
days.quote: Backbiting is permissible only when it is the necessary way to reach a valid, legitimate purpose.

quiz.question: Your friend is wronging someone. How do you support him?
options: Stand with him in the wrongdoing

quiz.question: You spoke about someone in his absence with something true of him that he dislikes. What is this?
You wrote a post hinting at someone's faults without naming him. Is that backbiting?
options: Yes, backbiting can be by speech, writing or gesture
No, as long as you didn't say the name
No, because it's on social media
quiz.explanation: Whether by speech, writing, gesture or hint.

askTheBook: What does it mean to support my brother when he is the wrongdoer?
What is the definition of backbiting?
When is backbiting permissible?

days.title: When Backbiting Is Permitted, and Dealing with Non-Muslims
days.question: When may I speak about someone in his absence? And how do I treat a peaceful non-Muslim?
days.principle: Backbiting is permitted for a legitimate purpose, for six reasons mentioned by Imam al-Nawawi; and kindness and justice are the foundation of the relationship with peaceful non-Muslims.

misconception.peopleSay: A non-Muslim has no rights, and I can wrong him or take what is his.
misconception.correct: Kindness and justice are the foundation of the relationship with peaceful non-Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ forbade wronging those under covenant and was severe about it, saying: «ألا من ظلم معاهدا أو انتقصه أو كلفه فوق طاقته أو أخذ منه شيئاً بغير طيب نفس فأنا حجيجه يوم القيامة».

days.action: If you have a peaceful non-Muslim neighbour or colleague, treat him today with kindness and fairness in one situation, as verse 8 of Surat al-Mumtahanah says.
lesson: The book continues the cases in which backbiting is permitted, among them identifying a person by a nickname he is known by without intending to belittle him, as the Prophet ﷺ used to call a man Dhul-Yadayn. But if the intention is to belittle, it is not allowed; the Prophet ﷺ corrected Aisha when she described a woman as short. Imam al-Nawawi gathered the reasons for permitting backbiting into six: seeking redress from oppression, seeking help to change a wrong, asking for a fatwa, warning Muslims against harm, someone who openly flaunts his sin, and identification. Then the book establishes that the foundation of our relationship with peaceful non-Muslims is kindness and justice. The Prophet ﷺ was very severe about wronging a person under covenant, and said he would be his opponent on the Day of Resurrection. In the last pages, the book begins to talk about consultation (shura), and that Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ, though infallible, to practise it so that people would follow his example.
days.quote: So He made kindness and justice the foundation of dealing with the peaceful among them.

quiz.question: Someone wronged you and you went to complain about him to a judge, telling what he did. Is that forbidden backbiting?
options: Yes, even if you were wronged
No, seeking redress is one of the cases in which backbiting is permitted
quiz.explanation: Seeking redress: the wronged person may complain of his wrong to the ruler, the judge and others.

quiz.question: Your neighbour is a peaceful non-Muslim. What is the basis of your dealing with him?
quiz.explanation: We believe that kindness and justice are the foundation of the relationship with peaceful non-Muslims.

quiz.question: You described someone by a physical trait to identify him to people, not to belittle him. What is the ruling?
options: Permissible if for identification and distinction; not permissible if to belittle
quiz.explanation: So it is established that mentioning such a thing for clarification and distinction is permissible; but if it is to belittle, it is not permissible.

askTheBook: In what cases is backbiting permissible?
How do I treat a peaceful non-Muslim?
What is the ruling on wronging a person under covenant?

days.title: Consultation, and Enjoining Good
days.question: Does Islam ask us to consult one another? And how do I change a wrong that I see?
days.principle: Consultation (shura) is the community's method and a foundation of governance within the sovereignty of the Shariah. Enjoining good and forbidding wrong is one of the greatest rites of Islam, and its obligation depends on having the ability and on the benefit outweighing the harm.

misconception.peopleSay: Consultation is something for government and politics only, and has nothing to do with the home.
misconception.correct: The obligation of consultation extends to family matters, including nursing a child and weaning him. Allah the Exalted said: «فإن أرادا فصالاً عن تراض منهما وتشاور فلا جناح عليهما».

days.action: In a small family decision today, consult your family before deciding, as the book says consultation extends to family matters.
lesson: Consultation in Islam is not only in governance; it reaches household matters like nursing a child and weaning him. The Prophet ﷺ consulted his Companions more than anyone, and the rightly guided caliphs followed the same way. Abu Bakr would search the Book of Allah first, then the Sunnah, and if he found nothing he would gather the leading Muslims and their scholars and consult them. Then the book moves to another obligation that protects the religion: calling to good and preventing evil as far as you are able and according to the benefit. The excellence of this Ummah rests on enjoining good, forbidding wrong and believing in Allah. The Prophet ﷺ set out the order for changing a wrong: by the hand; if unable, then by the tongue; and if unable, then by the heart.
days.quote: The Quran reciters were the members of 'Umar's council, whether old or young, and he always stopped at the limits of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

quiz.question: You saw a wrong and can change it neither with your hand nor with your tongue. What do you do?
options: Stay silent as if it's normal
Do what is beyond your ability whatever happens

quiz.question: If objecting to a wrong would bring a greater harm than the wrong itself, is objecting obligatory then?
options: Its obligation depends on ability and on the benefit outweighing the harm
quiz.explanation: And that its obligation depends only on having the ability and on the benefit outweighing the harm.

quiz.question: A Muslim ruler faces a new matter. What does he do first?
options: Decide by his own opinion alone
Refer to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, then consult the people of knowledge
quiz.explanation: When a matter came before Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, he would look in the Book of Allah…

askTheBook: What does consultation mean in Islam?
What are the levels of changing a wrong?
How did the rightly guided caliphs consult one another?

days.title: Seeking Knowledge and the Etiquette of Disagreement
days.question: I'm an ordinary person, not a specialist: where do I learn my religion from? And how do I deal with someone who differs with me on a question of fiqh?
days.principle: People are of three kinds in seeking knowledge: the layperson, the student of knowledge and the scholar. Questions open to reasoning (ijtihad) are not a basis for loyalty and disavowal; the one who differs is not to be pressured over them, and the community of Muslims may not split because of them.

misconception.peopleSay: Anyone who differs with me on a question of fiqh open to reasoning is an innovator, and I boycott him.
misconception.correct: Questions open to reasoning are not a basis for loyalty and disavowal; the one who differs is not to be pressured over them, nor is his religion to be impugned because of them, as long as his view came from reasoning or acceptable following.

days.action: If you have a question about your religion that you don't know the answer to, ask someone known for knowledge and piety today, and remember the hadith «إنما شفاء العي السؤال».
lesson: The book divides people in seeking knowledge into three. The layperson has no school of his own; his school is that of whoever gave him a fatwa, on condition that the mufti is known for knowledge and piety, and if fatwas differ he takes the fatwa of the more knowledgeable and more pious. The student of knowledge studies according to one of the four well-known schools and chooses books that pay attention to evidence until he advances. As for the scholar who has acquired the tools of ijtihad, he refers directly to the evidence. In the story of the Companion who performed ghusl and died, the Prophet ﷺ said that the cure for ignorance is asking. Then the book establishes that questions of reasoning with no definitive evidence are not made a basis for loyalty and disavowal, and we do not pressure the one who differs on them. If the one making ijtihad is right, he has two rewards, and if he errs, he has one reward.
days.quote: It was part of his ﷺ guidance that he did not rebuke any of those who differed in understanding his prohibition ﷺ of praying 'Asr except in Banu Qurayzah.

quiz.question: You're not a specialist, and you found two sheikhs who gave two different fatwas. What do you do?
options: Take the fatwa of the more knowledgeable and more pious
quiz.explanation: If the fatwas of the mujtahids differ for the layperson, he looks for whom to refer to, or takes the fatwa of the more knowledgeable and more pious.

quiz.question: Your friend follows a fiqh opinion of reasoning that differs from yours. How do you deal with him?
options: Don't pressure him and don't impugn his religion
quiz.explanation: The one who differs is not to be pressured over them, nor is his religion to be impugned because of them.

quiz.question: A scholar exercised ijtihad and erred. What is his ruling?
options: He is no longer considered a scholar
He has a reward for his ijtihad

askTheBook: What are the kinds of people in seeking knowledge?
What does a layperson do if fatwas differ?
How do we deal with disagreement on questions open to reasoning?

days.title: Islam Is Built on Five, and the First Is the Two Testimonies
days.question: What are the pillars of Islam? And why are the two testimonies of faith the first?
days.principle: Islam is built on five pillars. The two testimonies are the first obligation on those who are accountable and the first thing people are called to in the religion; by affirming them with belief and submission, the bond of Islam is established in this world and salvation from eternity in the Fire is attained in the Hereafter.

misconception.peopleSay: There could be more than one god in the universe and the world would run normally.
misconception.correct: A plurality of gods leads to conflict, each god taking away what he created, and some rising above others, which is utter corruption in the heavens and the earth. Allah the Exalted said: «لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا».

days.action: Renew the two testimonies today with your heart and tongue while understanding their meaning: that there is none truly worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger whom we must follow.
lesson: The second chapter of the book is about the five pillars of Islam, on which the Prophet ﷺ said Islam is built, and the whole Ummah agrees on this. The first pillar is the two testimonies: that we testify to Allah's oneness and to Muhammad ﷺ being His Messenger. Allah Himself testified that there is no god but Him, and the angels and those of knowledge testified with Him. He commanded His Prophet ﷺ and the whole Ummah to be certain of this without any doubt. The Quran explains that if there were more than one god, the universe would have been ruined, because each god would take what he created and rise above the other. That is why the Prophet ﷺ said that any servant who meets Allah with the two testimonies, without doubting them, will enter Paradise.
days.quote: So faith is not complete except by affirming the two testimonies, and Islam is not valid except with them.

quiz.question: What is the first obligation on any accountable person?
quiz.explanation: We believe that the two testimonies are the first obligation on those who are accountable.

quiz.question: Someone prays and fasts but does not affirm the two testimonies. Is his Islam valid?
options: No, there is no valid Islam without the two testimonies
quiz.explanation: So faith is not complete except by affirming the two testimonies, and Islam is not valid except with them.

quiz.question: Someone died saying the two testimonies without doubt. What destiny did the Prophet ﷺ give glad tidings of?
options: He will enter the Fire and remain there

askTheBook: What are the five pillars of Islam?
What is the status of the two testimonies in the religion?
Why is a plurality of gods impossible?

days.title: Muhammad ﷺ: Seal of the Prophets and Messenger to All the Worlds
days.question: Could a prophet come after our master Muhammad ﷺ? And is his message only for the Arabs?
days.principle: Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, so whoever claims a prophet after him is an apostate from Islam. He is the Messenger of Allah to all the worlds, so whoever claims the message of Islam addresses the Arabs alone has left Islam by that claim.

misconception.peopleSay: Islam is a religion for the Arabs only, and others are not required to follow it.
misconception.correct: Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah to all the worlds. Each prophet was sent to his own people specifically, while he was sent to all people. Whoever claims that the message of Islam addresses the Arabs alone has left Islam by that claim.

days.action: Memorise today the hadith of the brick and think about the image: a complete house missing one brick, and the Prophet ﷺ is the one who completed it.
lesson: A Muslim testifies that our master Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, so there is no prophet after him, and whoever claims a prophet after him has apostatised from Islam because he has belied the Quran and Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ likened himself among the prophets to a beautiful house missing one brick, and he is that brick that completed the building. Among his names is al-'Aqib, the one after whom there is no prophet, and he told 'Ali that he was to him as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after him. On this basis the book establishes that the Qadiani claim of prophethood for Mirza Ghulam Ahmad is apostasy, as major Islamic institutions have ruled. Also, the Prophet's ﷺ message is not only for the Arabs; it is for all the worlds. This is among his special qualities: every prophet before him was sent to his own people, and he was sent to all people.
days.quote: We testify that Muhammad is the Seal of the Prophets, so whoever claims a prophet after him is an apostate from Islam.

quiz.question: Someone claimed to be a prophet after our master Muhammad ﷺ, and people believed him. What is the ruling on those who believed him?
options: Fine if his miracles are strong
Apostates, because Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets
quiz.explanation: We testify that Muhammad is the Seal of the Prophets, so whoever claims a prophet after him is an apostate from Islam.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Islam is only for the Arabs." Is that right?
options: Right, and others have their own religions
No, the Prophet ﷺ was sent to all people
Only for the Arabs and the Persians

quiz.question: The Prophet ﷺ likened himself to the last brick in a house. What does that mean?
options: That he is the youngest of the prophets
That he is the Seal of the Prophets and the building was completed by him
That there are prophets after him
That he is a local prophet

askTheBook: What does it mean that the Prophet ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets?
What is the ruling on someone who claims prophethood after the Prophet ﷺ?
Is the message of Islam only for the Arabs?

days.title: Islam Abrogates What Came Before, and 'Isa Is Allah's Servant and Messenger
days.question: Does Allah accept any religion other than Islam after the Prophet ﷺ was sent? And what is our belief about 'Isa?
days.principle: The message of the Prophet ﷺ has abrogated the messages before it, and after his coming Allah accepts no religion from anyone except Islam. 'Isa is Allah's servant and messenger, His word which He conveyed to Maryam and a spirit from Him, and his example with Allah is like that of Adam.

misconception.peopleSay: The birth of 'Isa, peace be upon him, without a father proves he is not human.
misconception.correct: If 'Isa was born without a father, Adam was created without a father or a mother, and none of this proves that either of them is not human, for Allah the Exalted is able to do all of that.

days.action: Read verse 59 of Al 'Imran and reflect on its argument: if Adam was created without a father or mother, then creating 'Isa without a father is easier for Allah's power.
lesson: The book establishes that the Prophet's ﷺ message abrogated the messages before it and his Book abrogated the books before it, and after his coming Allah will not accept any religion other than Islam. Islam is the religion Allah perfected and was pleased with for His servants, and the verse commands the believers not to die except as Muslims, which requires hastening to Islam because one's appointed time is unknown. Then the book speaks about our master 'Isa: he is Allah's servant and messenger, His word conveyed to Maryam and a spirit from Him. The Quran answered those who went to excess about him by saying his example is like Adam's, created from dust, and Allah said to him "Be" and he was. The Quran also stressed that 'Isa and his mother used to eat food like other humans. 'Isa himself gave his people glad tidings of a messenger coming after him named Ahmad, and the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.
days.quote: So He informed us that Islam is the religion He perfected and was pleased with for His servants forever.

quiz.question: Someone says: "All existing religions lead to God after the Prophet ﷺ was sent." What is the correct understanding?
options: After his coming Allah accepts no religion other than Islam
quiz.explanation: So He informed us that Islam is the religion He perfected and was pleased with for His servants forever.

quiz.question: Someone is convinced of Islam but says: "I'll become Muslim later." What is required?
options: Wait until he is more certain
Become Muslim at the end of his life
Hasten immediately, because one's appointed time is unknown
quiz.explanation: This requires hastening to Islam immediately, because a person's appointed time is one of the matters of the unseen.

quiz.question: Someone says: "'Isa was born without a father, so he isn't human." What is the reply?
options: Adam was created without a father or a mother and he is human, so this is no proof of divinity
quiz.explanation: If 'Isa was born without a father, Adam was created without a father or a mother.

askTheBook: Does Allah accept a religion other than Islam?
What is the Muslims' belief about 'Isa, peace be upon him?
Whom did 'Isa, peace be upon him, give glad tidings of?

days.title: The Muslim Is Closer to the Messiah
days.question: Who is closest to the Messiah, peace be upon him: those who worshipped him, those who insulted him, or the Muslims?
days.principle: The Muslim is closer to the Messiah than those who worshipped him or insulted him, because he responded to what the Messiah gave glad tidings of, belief in Muhammad ﷺ, and because he neither went to excess about him like the Christians nor neglected him like the Jews.

misconception.peopleSay: Muslims have nothing to do with the Messiah, peace be upon him; he is the Christians' prophet only.
misconception.correct: The Muslim is closer to the Messiah than those who worshipped him or insulted him, because he responded to his glad tidings of Muhammad ﷺ and took the middle way between the one who exaggerated about him and the one who turned away from him.

days.action: Read the verses of Surat Maryam (30–36) in which 'Isa, peace be upon him, speaks in the cradle, and notice the first thing he said: "I am the servant of Allah."
lesson: The book explains that the Muslim is closer to the Messiah, peace be upon him, than those who worshipped him and those who insulted him. First, because the Muslim believed the glad tidings the Messiah brought of a prophet named Ahmad. Second, because he stood in the middle: he did not go to excess about him like the Christians who raised him to the rank of divinity, nor neglect him like the Jews who slandered his mother. The Quran declared Maryam innocent and described her as having guarded her chastity and believed in the words of her Lord, and that Allah chose her above the women of the worlds. The Quran ruled that those who said Allah is the Messiah have disbelieved, and told us that the Messiah himself told the Children of Israel to worship Allah, his Lord and theirs. The first thing 'Isa said in the cradle was: I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.
days.quote: Rather, he was guided in his matter to good speech, and so took the middle way between the one who exaggerated about him and the one who turned away from him.

quiz.question: Why is the Muslim closer to the Messiah than others?
options: Because he believed in him without excess or neglect, and responded to his glad tidings of Muhammad ﷺ
Because he considers him the son of God
quiz.explanation: That he responded to what the Messiah gave glad tidings of and called to: belief in Muhammad ﷺ.

quiz.question: Raising the Messiah to the rank of divinity is described as what?
quiz.explanation: Like the excess of the Christians who raised him to the rank of divinity.

quiz.question: How did 'Isa, peace be upon him, introduce himself in the cradle?
options: As the servant of Allah and His prophet

askTheBook: Why is the Muslim closer to the Messiah?
What is the Quran's position on Maryam?
What did 'Isa, peace be upon him, say in the cradle?

days.title: Purity Is Half of Faith
days.question: Why is purification so important in Islam? And how do I perform wudu and ghusl correctly?
days.principle: Purity is half of faith, and Allah does not accept prayer without purification. Purification from minor impurity is by wudu and from major impurity by ghusl, and when water is truly or effectively unavailable, tayammum suffices.

misconception.peopleSay: Ghusl from major impurity is only valid in one exact sequence.
misconception.correct: Ghusl as described in Aisha's hadith is the complete ghusl, but if he covers his whole body with water in any way, it suffices. Al-Shafi'i said: however the one bathing does it, it suffices if he washes his entire body.

days.action: Perform wudu today in the order given in the hadith of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, step by step, then pray two units and try not to let your mind wander in them.
lesson: Purification has a great status in Islam; the Prophet ﷺ said that purity is half of faith and the key to prayer, and Allah does not accept prayer without it. Allah even said to the Prophet ﷺ at the beginning of revelation: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾, because the polytheists did not purify themselves. Allah praised the people of the Quba' mosque because they loved to purify themselves, and that was cleaning themselves with water after relieving themselves. 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, taught people wudu as he saw the Prophet ﷺ do it: washing the hands, face and arms three times, wiping the head, and washing the feet. The complete ghusl is as in Aisha's hadith, but if a person covers his body with water in any way, it suffices. Tayammum is striking the ground with your palms and wiping your face and hands with them, as the Prophet ﷺ taught 'Ammar.
days.quote: Islam made purification the key to prayer and a condition of its validity, so no prayer is accepted without purification.

quiz.question: Someone prayed without wudu because he forgot. Is his prayer valid?
options: Yes, if his intention is good
No, no prayer is accepted without purification
quiz.explanation: Islam made purification the key to prayer and a condition of its validity, so no prayer is accepted without purification.

quiz.question: A traveller has no water at all, and the prayer time has come. What does he do?
options: Delay the prayer until he finds water
The prayer is dropped for him
quiz.explanation: When water is truly or effectively unavailable, tayammum suffices.

quiz.question: How is tayammum performed?
options: Strike the ground with your palms and wipe your face and hands
Wash the whole body with dust

askTheBook: How do I perform wudu like the Prophet ﷺ?
How is ghusl from major impurity performed?
When and how do I perform tayammum?
